definitions.name: Delay
definitions.code:
await context.sleep(Number(config.milliseconds ?? 1000));
return { value: inputs.value };
definitions.documentation:
# Delay

Waits before passing a value to the next step. This occupies a running node/worker; it is not a durable schedule or delayed-message queue.

## Sockets and configuration
- **exec** (control): optional execution gate.
- **value** (JSON Value, optional): payload to pass through.
- **value** (JSON Value): unchanged input after sleeping.
- **next** (control): automatic success route after the wait completes.
- **milliseconds** (number): fresh default 1000, schema minimum 0. The body also uses 1000 when the value is nullish.

## Example
Set milliseconds to 2000 and wire an upstream next to Execute. Wire this node's next to a follow-up operation, and its value to that operation's data input if needed. The downstream node becomes eligible only after the delay finishes and all other dependencies finish.

## Limits and failures
The runtime sleep API clamps a requested delay to 0–300,000 ms. The entire wait counts against the per-attempt node timeout; ensure that timeout is greater than the requested wait, allowing execution overhead. A retry repeats the wait from the beginning. Cancellation or host interruption does not preserve remaining sleep time or promise a later resume.

An absent optional value may disappear after serialization and cause a wired data consumer to skip; a next-only consumer can still follow the completed delay. No error route is declared. The body does no network I/O, secret access, logging or checkpoint writes. For periodic work, use a schedule/poll entry rather than keeping a worker asleep.

definitions.name: Remote receive
definitions.description: Continue when any matching remote sender runs in this workflow.
definitions.documentation:
Pair Remote send and Remote receive with the same case-sensitive Channel in Configuration. Channels are local to this canvas (each subflow instance has its own scope). These are ordinary routing nodes, not external triggers or code executors; they do not start another run.

Connect the branch's control output to Remote send Exec, and optionally supply Value. Matching receivers wait for all sender predecessors to settle and run once if at least one sender ran. Unselected senders do not block the join. Multiple receivers fan out. A channel needs both ends; cycles through remote links are rejected.

Remote receive Value is provided when exactly one sender ran, including false, zero, null and empty strings. Values is always an array of records with senderId and optional value for every active sender, in canvas node order. When several senders run, use Values rather than Value to avoid choosing a payload silently. Values use an explicit any boundary; connected destinations still validate their declared types. Errors remain available through context.errors in the same run.

Save and validate before running. Renaming a channel changes its routing; Undo restores the draft. Copying both ends retains the channel and therefore joins existing peers in the same canvas.

definitions.name: Text List
definitions.description: ONF typed decoder outputs v1. Text List
definitions.documentation:
# Text List

ONF typed decoder outputs v1.

Text List

Use this named type on matching Encode/Decode sockets. Values are JSON data;
this type performs no network request, model call, authentication, or business action.
Exact type ID and version must agree on both ends of a wire. JSON Schema rejects
incompatible values; formats are informational in ONF. Missing optional fields
and explicit null are different. Unknown fields remain lossless where permitted.
The matching codecs split useful properties or collection entries and reassemble
the original value. They never coerce strings/numbers or silently drop unknown data.

## Schema
```json
{
  "type": "array",
  "items": {
    "type": "string"
  }
}
```

## Example JSON value
```json
[]
```

Examples are synthetic. Null, collection, union and presence rules are defined by
the complete schema above; an empty example is not a claim every field is required.
Do not put credentials, tokens, or unnecessary business data into JSON records.

## Human Approval

Create a durable Inbox task and continue after an explicit version-guarded human decision.

The run stores its exact workflow and library versions, releases execution concurrency while waiting, and survives host restart. Completed upstream nodes are not repeated. Output `value` contains the resume payload (or null for a timer/timeout), `timedOut` reports event/approval expiry, and `next` continues execution. Approval values have `{decision,value}`; `taskId` identifies the Inbox task.

Event delivery requires a unique eventId and exact eventKey/correlationKey in the same workspace. Events match currently pending waits; they are not an unbounded pre-arrival event bus. definitions.name: Table Insert
definitions.description: Insert structured table rows with schema revision guards.
definitions.documentation:
# Table insert

Uses the authenticated workflow workspace and configured namespace/table. Requires ONF V2 with structured table support (F14). New installations do not contain this optional package.

Configure namespace, table and expectedSchemaRevision after reviewing Storage → Data → Schema. Inputs use the named Table insert request contract; result uses its named result contract. The node explicitly emits next after success. The server validates fields, required/null values, unique keys and row/schema versions. Update replaces the complete row data; omitted optional fields are removed. Read returns null for a missing row.

Rows retain stable keys, created/updated timestamps and increasing versions, including after deletion/reinsertion. Query supports AND filters (eq/ne/contains/gt/gte/lt/lte/isNull), stable insertion order and pages of at most 200 rows. A cursor is scoped to its workspace, namespace, table, filters and current data/schema revision. Restart paging after a mutation; do not replay writes automatically.

Every request commits independently. A Table Transaction request runs 1–100 insert/update/delete/query operations in order inside one synchronous SQLite transaction. This package node applies one configured table/schema revision to all nested operations; the lower-level context.storage(namespace).tables.transaction API also supports multiple tables in that namespace. Any failure rolls back all rows, versions, metadata and run-history captures in that batch. No transaction spans a node boundary, remote call, wait or workflow. A later node failure does not undo an earlier committed request.

10,000 distinct row keys per table (including version tombstones), 100 tables per namespace, 64 fields per schema, 256 KiB per row, 32 MiB total table data, 64 KiB per schema, 2 MiB per request/page and 8 MiB per transaction result. Encrypted server-side filtering currently scans a bounded table; it is not an indexed SQL analytics database. Schema changes retain historical schemas, reject incompatible rows and require reviewed workflow impact acknowledgements. Existing pins must be deliberately updated after a schema change. Dynamic code/input accesses cannot be exhaustively discovered. No credential, provider, network or direct filesystem calls occur in this node.
